headline: Sales rise while margin cuts squeeze profit
summary_short: CarMax's fiscal Q1 2027 (three months ended May 31, 2026, reported as this system's FY2026 Q2) net sales rose 6.2% y/y to $8,013.5M on higher used pricing and wholesale volume, but gross profit fell 4.4% to $854.4M and net earnings dropped 11.8% to $185.6M on continued margin-reduction pricing actions.
summary_long: Net sales rose 6.2% y/y to $8,013.5M on a 4.5% higher average used-vehicle price and 8.4% wholesale unit growth, while comparable-store used units fell 0.8%. Gross profit fell 4.4% to $854.4M as used gross profit per unit dropped $230 from last year's record amid continued margin-reduction pricing. SG&A fell 3.7% on lower compensation costs, but higher interest expense and a higher tax rate (28.2% vs 25.7%) pulled net earnings down 11.8% to $185.6M; diluted EPS fell 5.1% to $1.31, cushioned by a 6.9% smaller share count. Operating cash flow fell to $17.6M from $299.5M on inventory and loan-timing swings. FY2027 capex guidance was cut to ~$400M from $541M spent in FY2026; the $200M SG&A savings target was reaffirmed.

drivers.explanation: Used vehicle revenue rose 4.7% on a 4.5% higher average selling price (~$1,200); total used units were about flat. Wholesale revenue rose 14.0% on 8.4% more units plus 5.1% higher pricing.

Used gross profit fell 9.5% as gross profit per unit dropped $230 from last year's record high, reflecting continued pricing actions to drive unit sales; wholesale gross profit rose 8.3% on higher unit volume.
Not explained in the release — CarMax's income statement has no standalone EBIT line; this is a Yahoo timeseries-derived figure not reconciled or narrated in the filing.
Not explained in the release — EBITDA is not a filed subtotal; this is a Yahoo timeseries-derived figure not reconciled or narrated in the filing.
Net earnings fell 11.8% as the gross-profit decline and higher interest expense (revolver borrowings) outweighed 3.7% lower SG&A; the effective tax rate also rose to 28.2% from 25.7%.

Not explained in the release — CarMax's income statement has no standalone operating-income subtotal (CAF income sits above SG&A); this is a Yahoo timeseries-derived figure not reconciled in the filing.
Basic EPS fell only 5.1% versus an 11.8% net-income decline because basic weighted-average shares fell 6.7% y/y (152.1M to 141.8M) on prior-period buybacks, since paused.
Diluted EPS fell only 5.1% versus an 11.8% net-income decline because diluted weighted-average shares fell 6.9% y/y (152.6M to 142.1M) on prior-period buybacks, since paused.
Total cost of sales rose 7.6% y/y, growing faster than the 6.2% revenue increase as the cost-of-sales ratio rose to 89.3% from 88.2%, consistent with the used/wholesale gross-margin declines above.
Pretax income fell 8.7% on the gross-profit decline and higher interest expense, partly offset by the 3.7% SG&A reduction; the larger net-income decline reflects the higher effective tax rate.
Operating cash flow fell to $17.6M from $299.5M, primarily reflecting the year's smaller inventory decrease and the net change in auto loans held for investment and for sale, per the MD&A.
Capital expenditures fell 24.4% to $103.3M, continuing a planned pullback from elevated fiscal 2026 spending on offsite reconditioning/auction facilities and new stores as store-opening growth slows.
Diluted share count fell 6.9% y/y to 142.1M, reflecting stock repurchases executed earlier in fiscal 2026 before buybacks were paused in that year's fourth quarter.

Management's four-pillar strategy is showing "improved trends" — slight retail unit growth, SG&A leverage, higher CAF penetration and EPS trend gains — even as reported profit fell; a strategic update is planned for late fall.
